Composition
kŏm-pō-zĭsh´ŭn
n. (the prescribed formula of the holy oil and incense — Hebrew mathkoneth, a fixed proportion)
Latin compositio, a putting together. The Hebrew mathkoneth means a measured proportion or fixed formula — a recipe that may not be altered.

Biblical Definition

Composition in the Authorized Version means the exact prescribed formula of two holy things, and both times it appears God is forbidding imitation. Of the anointing oil: “Upon man's flesh shall it not be poured, neither shall ye make any other like it, after the composition of it: it is holy, and it shall be holy unto you” (Exo 30:32). Of the incense: “as for the perfume which thou shalt make, ye shall not make to yourselves according to the composition thereof: it shall be unto thee holy for the LORD” (Exo 30:37). The penalty is stated without qualification: “Whosoever compoundeth any like it, or whosoever putteth any of it upon a stranger, shall even be cut off from his people” (Exo 30:33). The oil itself was made by a specified art: “thou shalt make it an oil of holy ointment, an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary: it shall be an holy anointing oil” (Exo 30:25). Two principles are established. First, holy things are set apart by God's appointment, not by their ingredients — the same spices in another vessel are common. Second, God fixes the proportions of His own worship. Nothing here is left to the taste of the worshipper, and a man who improved on the formula was to be cut off.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines composition as the act of composing or putting together; the combination of ingredients in due proportion; a mixture or compound.

expand to see more

COMPOSI'TION, n. In a general sense, the act of composing, or that which is composed; the act of forming a whole by uniting parts.

2. The combination of distinct substances or ingredients; a mixture or compound.

3. The proportion or arrangement of the parts of a mixture; as, the composition of an ointment.

APOTH'ECARY, n. One who practices pharmacy; one who prepares drugs and compounds medicines.

Key Scripture

Exodus 30:32 — "Upon man's flesh shall it not be poured, neither shall ye make any other like it, after the composition of it: it is holy, and it shall be holy unto you."

Exodus 30:37 — "And as for the perfume which thou shalt make, ye shall not make to yourselves according to the composition thereof: it shall be unto thee holy for the LORD."

Exodus 30:33 — "Whosoever compoundeth any like it, or whosoever putteth any of it upon a stranger, shall even be cut off from his people."

Exodus 30:25 — "And thou shalt make it an oil of holy ointment, an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary: it shall be an holy anointing oil."

Modern Corruption

Worship is treated as an area of creative liberty, when Scripture fixes the composition of what God receives and cuts off the improver.

expand to see more

Exodus 30 is one of the plainest grounds of the regulative principle: what God has commanded in His worship is required, and what He has not commanded is not permitted. The oil and the incense were given by formula, and the man who reproduced them for other use was to be cut off from his people — not for wickedness in the ordinary sense, but for making a holy thing common. That is a severe doctrine and it is meant to be. It says that God fixes the terms on which He is approached, and that sincerity in the approacher settles nothing. Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire and died; Uzzah steadied the ark and died; the ground is the same.

The corresponding error is to conclude that God cares only about ceremony. He does not. The prophets pour scorn on incense offered by hands full of blood, and the same book that fixes the composition of the oil says obedience is better than sacrifice. Both stand. God appoints the manner of His worship, and God demands the heart of the worshipper, and a church that keeps the second while inventing freely in the first has claimed a liberty Exodus never granted. The apostolic rule for the New Testament assembly runs the same way: let all things be done decently and in order, and let all things be done unto edifying, by what Christ appointed and not by what pleases the congregation.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew mathkoneth (H4971), measurement, prescribed proportion — Exodus 30:32, 37; roqach (H7548), a compounded perfume; raqach (H7543), to compound as an apothecary.

expand to see more

Hebrew mathkoneth (H4971) — a fixed proportion or formula; Exodus 30:32 and 30:37, and Ezekiel 45:11 of just measures.

Hebrew raqach (H7543) — to compound as an apothecary; Exodus 30:25, 33.

Hebrew karath (H3772) — to cut off; the penalty for reproducing the holy composition.

Hebrew qodesh (H6944) — holiness, that which is set apart; the reason given for the whole prohibition.

The ingredients were common spices; what made the oil holy was God's appointment, not the materials.

Usage

"“Neither shall ye make any other like it, after the composition of it”."

"“Whosoever compoundeth any like it… shall even be cut off”."

"“It shall be unto thee holy for the LORD” — set apart by appointment, not by ingredients."
